statements: There is no general statutory definition of "shop" in Scots law: each Act that uses the word defines it for its own purposes and the definitions differ from each other.
Sections 38 and 39 of the Shops Act 1950 are repealed and must not be presented as current law or as provisions that are in force.

Section 7 of the Christmas Day and New Year's Day Trading (Scotland) Act 2007 defines "shop" as any premises within a building where there is carried on a trade or business consisting wholly or mainly of the retail sale of goods, and "large shop" as a shop with a relevant floor area exceeding 280 square metres.

Section 232(3) of the Employment Rights Act 1996 provides that "shop" includes any premises where any retail trade or business is carried on, with section 232(4) treating only the retail part of mixed-use premises as the shop.

Section 43ZB(2)(a) of the Employment Rights Act 1996 carries a second, different definition for the purposes of its own Part, under which "shop" means any premises where there is carried on a trade or business consisting wholly or mainly of the sale of goods, not the retail sale of goods.
